summary: A/B testing beta: Console experiment latency p95 doesn't match customer dashboard (AcmeAI)
description:
Issue summary
- AcmeAI (beta partner) reports the A/B testing results page in Console shows materially lower p95 latency for Variant B than their internal dashboard for the same route/time window.
- Concern: trust in experiment reporting; risk of making rollout decisions based on incorrect data.

Customer report (from ticket intake)
- Project: acmeai-prod
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming enabled)
- Experiment: exp_01J1ZP2X6Q2R1R ("support-bot-model-compare")
- Variants:
  - A (control): rw-openchat-3.5 @ fp16
  - B (treatment): rw-openchat-3.5 @ int8 (optimized)
- Console shows (last 6h):
  - Variant A p95 E2E latency: ~690ms
  - Variant B p95 E2E latency: ~480ms
- AcmeAI internal dashboard (client-side, same 6h):
  - Variant A p95: ~740ms
  - Variant B p95: ~720ms
- They also noted TTFT looks closer between systems than E2E.

Impact
- Customer uncertainty about whether optimization changes actually improved latency.
- No evidence of production degradation; this is a reporting mismatch.

Environment
- Hosted API, prod
- Observed primarily in us-east; eu-west looked closer but still inconsistent.
- Streaming responses (SSE) used for the route under test.

Initial triage notes (Support / Solutions)
- Asked customer for:
  - Exact time range + timezone
  - Definition of latency in their dashboard (TTFT vs full stream completion)
  - Whether their p95 is computed on client wall time including network
  - Request IDs sample (10–20) for spot-checking
  - Whether they filter by region, model, route, and experiment/variant consistently

Investigation timeline

2026-03-08 (Support - Simran Kaur)
- Reproduced discrepancy internally using Console results view for the experiment and comparing to raw request logs.
- Noted Console graph label shows "End-to-end latency" and tooltip says "request start to response end".
- Pulled sample request IDs from AcmeAI:
  - Observed that customer’s client timing includes duration until stream completion (last token received), which is expected to be higher than TTFT.
- However, Console E2E numbers appeared closer to TTFT than to true stream completion time.

2026-03-09 (Telemetry - Logan Wright, with Nadia Rahman + Caleb Johnson)
- Checked metrics definitions per schema v1:
  - ttft_ms: time from gateway receiving request -> first token flushed
  - e2e_ms: time from gateway receiving request -> response finished (for non-streaming) OR stream finished (for streaming)
- Queried raw gateway spans in prod for a handful of request_ids:
  - Found that for streaming requests, the span field being exported into the experiment aggregation dataset for "e2e" was populated with response_start / headers_sent timestamp, not stream_end.
  - This made "e2e" effectively equal to TTFT (+ small overhead) in the aggregated experiment tables, leading to underreported E2E.

2026-03-10 (Eng - Mina Haddad + Amara Diallo)
- Root cause confirmed:
  - API gateway emitted correct TTFT, but the "request_end" used by the experiment results aggregation was sourced from access log completion that terminates when headers are committed for streaming endpoints (SSE), not when the stream closes.
  - This only affected the dataset powering the Console A/B results view (per-experiment aggregation). Other internal latency dashboards that use full request spans were not impacted.
- Scope:
  - Only impacts streaming routes where customers interpret E2E as "until last token".
  - Affects both variants equally in distribution, but can distort comparisons if token output lengths differ across variants.

2026-03-11 (Fix plan)
- Short-term mitigation:
  - Updated customer with accurate definitions and advised comparing TTFT in Console until fix ships.
  - Provided a recommended way to compare full stream duration from raw request logs (internal-only query shared by Support).
- Product/UX follow-up drafted:
  - Add explicit metric selector text: "TTFT" vs "Stream duration (until final token)".
  - Add warning banner when E2E is computed from incomplete stream-end timestamps (beta guardrail).

2026-03-12 (Resolution)
- Deployed backend fix to use stream_end / response_completed timestamp for streaming requests in the experiment results pipeline.
- Rebuilt/backfilled experiment aggregates for AcmeAI experiment exp_01J1ZP2X6Q2R1R for the last 7 days.
- Post-fix validation:
  - Console E2E p95 aligned with AcmeAI client dashboard within expected network overhead (+/- ~30–80ms depending on region).
  - TTFT remained consistent pre/post.

Customer-facing update (sent via Support)
- Confirmed the mismatch was due to a beta reporting bug for streaming E2E latency.
- Explained metric definitions:
  - TTFT: server-side time to first token
  - E2E (streaming): server-side time until stream completion (last token)
  - Client dashboards may include network and client buffering
- Notified that Console results were backfilled and should now match more closely.
- Requested they re-check with the same window and region filter; offered to review any remaining deltas with request IDs.

Internal comments (selected)
- Logan Wright (Telemetry): "Confirmed dataset powering Console A/B results is using response_start for streaming. Needs to use stream_end; current E2E ~= TTFT, so label is misleading. Fix + backfill." 
- Nadia Rahman (Metering): "If E2E is wrong, cost attribution still OK; but any 'cost per second' derived numbers will be off. No billing impact." 
- Allison Grant (Observability): "Please add validation test for streaming route: e2e_ms must be >= ttft_ms + threshold for non-trivial outputs." 

Resolution
- Status set to Resolved after:
  - Pipeline fix deployed
  - Backfill completed for impacted experiments
  - Customer confirmed results are now consistent with their internal view (allowing for network overhead)

Workarounds (while fix was pending)
- Compare TTFT in Console (accurate) rather than E2E.
- Use raw request logs/trace spans to compute stream duration where needed.

Follow-ups / action items
- Add automated regression test in results aggregation job for streaming endpoints (e2e_ms sanity vs ttft_ms).
- Update Console copy/tooltips to distinguish TTFT vs stream completion clearly (beta).
- Add release note entry to beta changelog: "Fixed E2E latency reporting for streaming experiments."
